rv.q: But after an evening in this headache-inducingly loud and bright fantasy, you may well be wishing you were home, along with Dorothy.
It all feels a bit hollow beneath the shiny exterior, like the Tin Man’s chest cavity.
Effectively, the time-honoured appeal of L Frank Baum’s story carries the day, and what must keep us sated is the theatrical spectacle.
But her streetwise Dorothy is no ingenue, and I did miss the vulnerability that is one of the character’s obstacles to overcome.
Yet Foster’s production of this most enchanting of stories is efficient rather than inspired.
With its revisionist take Wicked defying gravity and still pulling in audiences after many years just over Green Park, it looks like audiences will be flocking to Oz in droves this summer.
Between a committed cast and those enduringly glorious songs, this is still wonderful family fun.
Few will feel shortchanged by a show that offers great songs, real spectacle and a sprinkling of starry talent.
It is very family friendly and audience reaction marks it a crowd pleaser.
This fresh take on a classic remains faithful to the story we all know and love but gives it so much more.
The warmth of her smile, and soaring vocals in Somewhere over the Rainbow will pierce your heart.

cn.t: Foster's high-octane revival dazzles with extravagant visuals and Onuorah's standout Dorothy, but critics are divided on its relentlessly busy, steampunk-infused approach—some find it exhilarating family fun, others exhausting spectacle over substance.
